sents.t: In August, Ana taught a free first-aid class at the community center, and I signed up with Lily and Carlos.
As a manager, I’m responsible for my team, so I wanted to know what to do in an emergency.
“Most emergencies happen at home or at work,” Ana began.
“If you know a few simple steps, you might save a life.”
First, we learned what to do if someone is choking.
“If the person can cough, let them cough,” Ana said.
“If they can’t breathe or speak, stand behind them and push hard above their stomach.” We practiced on each other, very gently.
Then we learned CPR on plastic dummies.
“If someone collapses and isn’t breathing, call 911 first. Then push hard and fast in the middle of the chest.” We had to push to the rhythm of an old disco song.
Carlos started singing, and everyone laughed.
We also learned how to treat burns.
“If you burn your hand, hold it under cool water for twenty minutes. Don’t put ice or butter on it!”
At the end, we each received a certificate.
On Monday, I hung mine next to the first-aid kit at the bookstore.
“If anything happens, I’ll know what to do,” I told my team.
I hope I’ll never need it.
